explanation: For strictly increasing integers, values[i] - i is nondecreasing. Binary search this difference for zero, returning any matching index. Widen the subtraction to avoid overflow.
timeComplexity: O(log n). A sign comparison discards at least half the candidate indices each iteration.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Only endpoints and a difference accumulator are needed.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Because the input integers are strictly increasing, values[i]-i is nondecreasing. A negative difference at middle excludes all positions to its left; a positive difference excludes all positions to its right. Binary search therefore retains every possible zero, returning an index exactly when one exists.
walkthrough: For [-3,-1,2,6], midpoint 1 has difference -1-1=-2, so search to its right. At index 2 the difference is 2-2=0, so return 2. The judge accepts this original index as a witness.
edgeCases: A match at index 0 is valid.
Several matching indices may exist; any one is accepted.
Strictly increasing distinct values are required for the monotone difference.
